# TSMP Core 0.3.0-beta.2

This beta consolidates component Send Mode, decoder consistency and memory improvements, synchronization fixes, and the codec preparation API. The stable release remains 0.2.0.

## Added: Component Send Mode

Choose how each TSMPNetworkBehaviour sends automatic TransSync fields, directly in its Inspector:

- **Default** preserves the component author's per-field SendOnChange settings.
- **On Change** filters unchanged values and periodically refreshes them.
- **Always** repeats unchanged values, useful when stationary Transform or paused Timeline state should be resent more often.

Mode changes take effect without Apply Setup or a binding rebuild. Minimum intervals, eligibility, priority and payload capacity still apply. Always uses more bandwidth; it does not guarantee delivery or raise priority. RPCs and manual Writer calls are unchanged.

## Fixed and Improved

- Decode header, calibration and payload from one frozen Float32 image, avoiding mismatched asynchronous reads.
- Reuse decoder payload capacity, bound parsing to valid bytes and reject empty or truncated network payloads.
- Filter older and duplicate frames using wrap-aware ordering. Add a receiver-local **Window Size**, default 256, for frame-zero restart handling.
- Correct reentrant RPC queue accounting and reject RPCs that cannot fit the payload. Retransmission remains a finite attempt budget, not acknowledged delivery.
- Honor Receive Interpolation None before decoding fields and clear pending Rigidbody velocities when physics reception is disabled.
- Invalidate stale BlendShape targets, respect receiver Animator layer selections, and correct Animator drift and negative state-hash handling.
- Safely reduce avatar pool limits while retaining inactive objects for reuse.
- Commit avatar root delta and keepalive state only after successful output through the new opt-in TransSync.SentEvent callback.
- Remove redundant Setup Editor output copies, preserve integer-sized texture blocks and clear remainder pixels.
- Pace FFmpeg output independently of incoming texture updates while retaining the latest frame.

## Codec API and Updating

- Add TSMPCodec.PrepareDecode, GetDecodeSampleSize and calibration-LUT helpers. Existing codecs can keep the default no-op preparation path. Core does not select codec-specific algorithms.
- Codecs using the new preparation API require Core 0.3.0-beta.2. Install Core first; optimized codec releases are separate packages, not included automatically in this release.
- VCC: enable prerelease versions in the repository at https://vpm.kiba.red/ and select Core 0.3.0-beta.2. Ordinary Unity continues to use UPM without requiring VRCSDK.
- Allow Unity to refresh bindings and recompile UdonSharp programs after updating. Existing components default to Send Mode Default, preserving their field settings.
- English, Korean and Japanese documentation has been updated.

## Datagram and Receiver Compatibility

The protocol version and datagram are unchanged: a **56-byte header followed by the existing payload**. No window, session or Send Mode bytes are added.

| Byte range | Field | Encoding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 20..23 | StreamId | UInt32 little-endian |
| 24..27 | FrameIndex | UInt32 little-endian |
| 28..31 | TimestampMs | UInt32 little-endian; not used for ordering |
| 44..49 | Reserved | Six zero bytes |
| 52..55 | Header CRC32 | UInt32 little-endian over bytes 0..51 |

The skipDuplicateFrames option now also filters older frames. Frame zero can restart ordering once the previous index reaches Window Size. This is a heuristic, not a session ID: delayed old zero frames, missing reset frames and early restarts remain ambiguous. RPC deduplication is unchanged.

## Validation and Known Limits

Unity 2022.3.22f1, Windows/Direct3D11, RTX 4090; Worlds SDK 3.10.4-beta.2 with bundled UdonSharp. Texture tests used local Luma4 0.0.4-beta.1 candidate sources.

- Passed native and SDK Editor scheduling, live mode switching, Editor encoding and actual compiled Encoder Udon VM tests.
- Passed Gamma GPU loopback in Play Mode and an actual Windows x64 Mono Player, including Transform, animated Humanoid/Timeline, Unicode and RPCs. The Player build had zero errors and 16 existing shader warnings.
- Passed the same 11-frame native Gamma Play Mode loopback with the existing Luma4 0.0.3 release checkout.
- Passed fresh full UdonSharp client compilation, shared Controller binding setup and a local SDK world bundle build.
- Passed English, Korean and Japanese website builds and TypeScript checks.

The full legacy **Linear** loopback harness still fails its CPU calibration/block-expansion check (`Calibration symbols 0 and 1 are too close.`); separate Linear Editor encoding checks pass. Live VRChat client execution, built-world proxy/backing reference behavior, Quest, IL2CPP and managed stripping are **not verified**. The reviewed reference-serialization risks are not claimed as fixed by this release.

[Detailed validation and evidence](https://github.com/kibalab/TSMP-Core/blob/v0.3.0-beta.2/Validation~/RELEASE-0.3.0-beta.2.md)
